name: phone-settings
description: Settings that come up from the bottom on a phone and swipe down to close. litt's Dialog does this by itself on compact screens (since the responsive motion build), so the test is whether the agent installs and composes it instead of building its own sheet.
prompt:
The home page of this app is still the Vite starter. Replace it with a simple home for the studio (the litt.design wordmark, a heading and a line of intro) and put a Settings button top right. Clicking it opens settings with a display name, an email, and a checkbox for whether I get an email when a build finishes. Save and Cancel at the bottom. Save can just close it and show a quick confirmation on the page.

I mostly use this on my phone, so there it should feel native: it comes up from the bottom of the screen and I can swipe it down to close it. On a laptop a normal dialog is fine.

This is for litt.design, our own studio site, not a client job, so make the calls yourself. Make sure it builds and looks right in light and dark.
look:
Judge the page-* screenshots (the home page as loaded, light and dark, 1440 and 390 wide), the open-* screenshots (after clicking Settings, 1440 wide), the open-phone-* screenshots (after tapping Settings on a 390 wide touch screen; open-phone-light-390.png and open-phone-dark-390.png are settled, and the ones ending in -60ms, -140ms and -260ms are frames taken that long after the tap) and the swiped-* screenshots (the same open panel at 390, after it was dragged down 360px from its title). Claims:
1. page: the home page is real studio content (a wordmark, a heading and a line of intro), not the Vite starter, with a visible Settings button at the top right at 1440 and at 390. A Settings icon, if there is one, sits on the same line as its label.
2. open at 1440: a panel floats in the middle of the page, which is dimmed or tinted. It has a title such as Settings, a display name field, an email field and a build-emails checkbox with a visible text label. Save and Cancel are at the bottom right, Save last. Save is the only accent-filled button and Cancel has no color fill. The panel has slightly rounded corners (about 10px), a hairline edge and a soft glow or shadow with no hard offset.
3. open-phone, settled: the panel is anchored to the bottom edge of the screen and spans the full width or very nearly. It is a sheet that rises from the bottom, not a card floating in the middle with space on all four sides. Its top corners are slightly rounded (about 10px), the page behind is dimmed or tinted, and the display name, email, checkbox, Save and Cancel are all fully visible with nothing cut off.
4. open-phone, settled: every field has its label above it, the inputs are roomy (about 44px tall), and Save and Cancel sit at the bottom of the sheet with Save last. Save is the only accent-filled button.
5. open-phone frames: the sheet travels up from the bottom. In the -60ms frame it sits clearly lower than in the settled shot (partly or fully below the bottom edge), and in the -140ms frame it is closer to its place. A panel that is already in its final place at 60ms, or that fades or grows in at the middle of the screen, fails.
6. swiped: dragging the open panel down closed it. In the swiped screenshots the panel is gone, or at least mostly off the bottom of the screen, and the home page behind it is clearly visible and no longer dimmed. A panel still open in its original place fails.
7. All screenshots: no text is bold (reading text is regular, headings and labels only a touch heavier), there are no emoji, no decorative gradients and no hard offset shadows. The keyboard focus outline, the primary button's blue gradient fill (no glow) and the one soft light from the top (litt's light source, a faint tint that fades down a surface, once per view) are allowed. In the dark screenshots the panel's edge, its text and its fields are clearly legible, and the panel is set off from the page behind it.
